name: Coast Funds Stewardship Project Funding
summary: Standing funding for participating First Nations, and the stewardship offices and societies acting for them, to run conservation projects such as monitoring, habitat and coastal restoration and protected-area management in the Great Bear Coast region.

geography.label: Great Bear Rainforest, Great Bear Sea and Haida Gwaii

steps: Monthly review (up to $150,000) or quarterly review (over $150,000)

eligibility.rule: The project is performed by or on behalf of a First Nation.
The recipient is a qualified donee, except a non-qualified donee providing required information and documentation.
The application is endorsed in writing by the First Nation's band council or other acceptable governing body.
The endorsement confirms a favourable evaluation of the project's conservation benefits.
The conservation project is in the Project Area, except capacity building for prospective initiatives within it.
A protected-area project is consistent with all approved management plans for that area.
An EBM project is consistent with legal objectives adopted through ministerial order or regulatory power.
Project activities are consistent with provincial laws, regulations, determinations, and policies.

documents: Council or Board resolution of support
Detailed capital expenditure budget with valid quotations, if infrastructure
Detailed multi-year operating and maintenance budget, if infrastructure

status.quote: Participating First Nations can apply to access funding through Coast Funds at any time during the year.

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include: The governing bodies of participating First Nations specified in related agreements that are listed as a qualified donee with the Canada Revenue Agency Stewardship offices, resource management departments, or non-profit societies with delegated responsibility for conservation on behalf of a participating First Nation.

geography.quote: focused on sustaining or enhancing the ecological integrity of the Great Bear Rainforest, Great Bear Sea, and Haida Gwaii (the Project Area, also known as the Great Bear Coast)

access.quote: Participating First Nations can apply to access funding through Coast Funds at any time during the year.

window.quote: Participating First Nations can apply to access funding through Coast Funds at any time during the year.

effort.quote: A complete application includes all supporting documents identified above. Applications up to $150,000 are reviewed on a monthly basis and approved by Coast Funds' senior leadership team.
Applications for more than $150,000 are reviewed on a quarterly basis and approved by the Project Review Committee (up to $1 million) or the Board of Directors (over $1 million).

eligibility.quote: Projects must be performed by or on behalf of a First Nation.
Project recipients must be listed as "qualified donees" by the Canada Revenue Agency, except in the case of a non-qualified donee that has provided, and will provide the information and documentation
All applications for funding must first be endorsed in writing by the First Nation's band council or other acceptable governing body.

The First Nation's endorsement must also confirm it has conducted an evaluation of the project with results that favourably confirm the viability of conservation benefits that will result from the activities to be conducted with the funding.

Conservation projects (i.e. habitat restoration, conservancy management) that occur outside the Project Area except where projects are focused on capacity building specific to prospective conservation initiatives (i.e. certified training, workforce development) within the Project Area
Projects in Protected Areas not consistent with all approved management plans for the area
Conservation/stewardship projects in respect of EBM must be consistent with any legal objectives adopted through Ministerial order or regulatory power.
Activities inconsistent with provincial laws, regulation, determinations, or policies

after_award.quote: For all approved projects, recipients are required to provide sign off on a final report following completion of the project that provides:

documents.quote: Project plan Council and/or Board resolution of support for accessing the funds for the purposes of the application
A detailed capital expenditure budget for the infrastructure investment, including valid quotations for materials and construction;
A detailed multi-year operating and maintenance (O&M) budget to support the infrastructure.
